Abstract:

The rapid advancement of the Internet of Things (IoT) and Industrial Internet of Things (IIoT) has enabled intelligent applications across smart cities, healthcare, industrial automation, and smart energy systems. However, secure and efficient communication remains challenging due to resource-constrained devices, insecure communication channels, and distributed fog computing environments. This thesis proposes lightweight authentication and key agreement protocols for IoT, fog computing, and IIoT using Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC), one-way hash functions, symmetric cryptography, and XOR operations to achieve strong security with low computational and communication overhead. The proposed work includes an ECC-based two-factor authentication scheme for fog computing, a sustainable mutual authentication protocol for IoT&ndashFog&ndashCloud environments, a lightweight machine-to-machine authentication protocol for IIoT, and a three-factor authentication protocol for the Smart Home environment. Formal verification using ProVerif, BAN logic, and the RoR model, along with informal analysis, confirms resistance against various attacks. Performance evaluation and iFogSim simulations demonstrate that the proposed schemes provide secure, lightweight, efficient, and sustainable authentication suitable for next-generation IoT and IIoT environments.
